Path App is a Hack Western 13 project. The deadline is Sun Nov 22, 2026, 9:00 a.m. Toronto time, and judges see the site on laptops at the booth. People scan a place (a building, campus, trail or event venue) with a LiDAR iPhone, upload it, and share a 3D map by link or QR as Public, Unlisted or Private. Visitors open it signed out. It is community maps for any place, not just events: the uploader is called the "map owner", never "organizer". The only exceptions are the real Hack Western organizers and the "Organizers' Choice" prize. Team: Sam (API, issue #3), Krishna and Anish (phone capture, #4), Anish (second-phone trial, #5). Arielle owns all frontend UI/UX.

Design direction is in `apps/web/DESIGN.md`. Colors: cream paper `#F3EBD0`, forest `#2F4A3A`, coral `#F48057` used only as a fill (never as text), rust `#A8421F` for coral-looking text, night `#121C16` behind 3D. Fonts: Overpass for display, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for body. The landing hero is a live point-cloud scan that assembles from scattered dots, a coral route that draws itself, and footprints, plus a QR code. The playbook artifact is https://claude.ai/artifact/Abt1dfRD8khy9gxW5pDNJV (open it with the Artifact read action). The synthetic scan fixture is `fixtures/venue/scene.ply`. content.content:
# Path web design direction Owner: Arielle. This is the agreed visual and UX direction for the landing page and the app in `apps/web/`. The live, interactive version (hero prototype, flip cards, footprint trail, guest-view mockup) is the playbook artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/Abt1dfRD8khy9gxW5pDNJV (private to Arielle until shared). ## Color Cream is the page background, green is the main UI color, coral is the accent. | Token | Hex | Role | | --- | --- | --- | | `paper` | `#F3EBD0` | Page background (primary) | | `surface` | `#FAF5E6` | Cards and sheets on top of paper | | `forest` | `#2F4A3A` | Primary: text, headings, buttons, active states | | `coral` | `#F48057` | Accent: route line, pins, highlights, CTA button fill | | `rust` | `#A8421F` | Coral-colored text and links (coral itself fails as text) | | `night` | `#121C16` | Background of every 3D view and dark landing bands | | `sage` | `#A9C4AE` | Primary color in dark mode, contour lines | | `ink` | `#15221B` | Text on coral buttons | | `muted` | `#5E6B60` | Secondary text on paper (4.7:1) | Contrast rules, measured with WCAG ratios: - Forest on paper 8.1:1. Use for all body text. - Coral on paper is 2.2:1 and white on coral is 2.6:1. Never use coral for text or put white text on coral. - Coral buttons use ink text (6.3:1). Coral-flavored text uses rust (5.1:1). - Point clouds wash out on cream. Render 3D on `night`. Coral on night is 6.7:1, which suits the route line and 3D labels. ## Type - Display: **Overpass** 800–900 (based on Highway Gothic road-sign lettering). - Body and UI: **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** (Braille Institute, designed for low-vision readers). - Data: **Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono** for coordinates, distances, share IDs. - Avoid a soft serif. Cream + coral + serif reads as a generic generated landing page. ## Motifs and motion - The landing hero is the product: the real scan assembles from scattered points, the coral route draws itself, footprints walk it to a destination pin. Use the fixture until a real scan exists. - Footprints are the landing-page motif: one SVG path in the left gutter, prints revealed with scroll (GSAP ScrollTrigger + MotionPath). Under 40% opacity. - Inside the app, routes are a coral line with flowing dashes and waypoint dots, not footprints, since some users roll rather than walk. - One orchestrated animation per landing section. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` everywhere. - Booth: a QR in the hero and Join section opens the guest link on the judge's phone. The hero replays after ~20 s idle. ## Landing page sections Hero (live scan + QR + Log in / Sign up) → The problem (sticky scroll: 2D floor plan tilts into 3D, one measured stat) → Our product (Scan · Share with Public/Unlisted/Private · Navigate with landmark cues, real screenshots) → How to use (3 steps joined by footprints) → Creators (flip cards: hover on desktop, tap on iPhone, focus on keyboard; GitHub, LinkedIn, résumé, portfolio) → Join us (trail ends at a pin by the CTA and QR). ## App screens, by priority - **P0:** guest view at `/s/:shareId` (full-bleed 3D on night, destinations in a bottom sheet, Gemini cue card with source frame and "approved by the map owner", route by Dijkstra over the manifest graph) · upload with visibility toggle, copy link and QR · Gemini cue review (accept / edit / reject) · landing hero. - **P1:** rest of the landing page · Explore (public scans + filter chips: Campus, Events, Hospitals, Trails, Step-free) · settings (step-free routing, text size, reduce motion) · one "elevator out" alert that reroutes. - **Cut or fake:** custom login screens (use the provider's hosted login), comments and feed, events calendar, live indoor positioning. ## Stack Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + React Router, built to static files. | Job | Library | | --- | --- | | 3D viewer | `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei` (PLYLoader, CameraControls, Line, Html) | | Scroll story, footprints | `gsap`, `@gsap/react` (ScrollTrigger, MotionPath, DrawSVG) | | UI motion | `motion` | | Landing smooth scroll | `lenis` (off in the app and under reduced motion) | | Components | shadcn/ui (Radix) | | Bottom sheet | `vaul` | | Toasts, QR, icons | `sonner`, `qrcode.react`, `lucide-react` | | Showpieces | Two or three restyled snippets from Magic UI, Aceternity UI or React Bits | Mobile targets: the guest link opens signed out in under 3 s on an iPhone; cap device pixel ratio at 2 and downsample large PLYs. Hosting is proposed on Vultr behind Caddy, which must serve `index.html` for `/s/` so direct links don't 404. ======== # Website Arielle owns the website: the signed-in home, upload and sharing, and the guest 3D viewer. Build the website here. Start with an upload control, the three visibility choices, a copy-link action and a guest route at `/s/`. Display upload, loading and processing failures where they occur. For the first integration, upload the sample PLY as **Unlisted**, open the returned link in a signed-out session, and use the response’s `assetPath` to load the point cloud with vertex colors. A guest should be able to orbit the scene and recognize the corridor junction. Use the actual phone export to choose camera framing, point size and mobile performance targets. The local API provides fixture bytes and exercises sharing rules. Replace its test page with the website’s guest route during integration. [Local API commands](../../services/api/README.md) · [Capture format and viewer notes](../../docs/scan-formats.md) ## Run locally Requires Node 22+ and pnpm. The dev server proxies `/api` to the scan mock on `127.0.0.1:8001`. ```sh py -3 -B tools/scan_mock.py --port 8001 # from the repo root (or: make dev-api) cd apps/web && pnpm install && pnpm dev # http://localhost:5173 ``` Open `http://localhost:5173/maps` (Your maps), then **New map** (`/maps/new`), choose `fixtures/venue/scene.ply`, pick a visibility and upload. The page shows the guest link, a copy button and a QR code, and lets you change visibility or private viewers afterwards. You can also upload with the curl command in the [API README](../../services/api/README.md). Then open `http://localhost:5173/s/`. The guest page sends no `X-Dev-User` header, so it is a signed-out guest. Owner calls (upload, sharing) send `X-Dev-User: demo-owner` in development only (override with `VITE_DEV_USER`). A production build sends none, because the hosted API reads the signed-in session. `pnpm build` type-checks and writes static files to `dist/`. `pnpm preview` serves them with the same proxy on port 4173. The host must serve `index.html` for `/s/`. | Path | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/index.css` | Color and type tokens from [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) as a Tailwind v4 `@theme`. | | `src/lib/shares.ts` | Calls `GET /api/shares/` and its asset. The API answers 404 both for unknown and for denied shares, so the guest sees one state. | | `src/lib/ply.ts` | Parses ASCII or binary PLY with `PLYLoader`, rejects empty or non-finite scans, keeps at most 600k points. | | `src/components/ScanViewer.tsx` | Colored points on `night`, DPR capped at 2, orbit (one finger turns, two fingers zoom and pan), framed from behind the entrance (+Z). Loaded lazily alongside the metadata request. | | `src/components/AppLayout.tsx` | Signed-in shell: forest sidebar (My maps, Community, New map, account) on desktop, top bar and bottom tab bar on phones. | | `src/routes/MyMaps.tsx` | `/maps`: your maps (`GET /api/scans/mine`) and maps shared with you (`GET /api/scans/shared`), with All, Public, Unlisted, Private and Shared with me filters. Each card's ⋯ menu offers Copy link, Manage map and Delete… (with a confirmation). | | `src/routes/ManageMap.tsx` | `/maps/:shareId`: rename, link and QR code, change who can open it, and delete. Only for the map's owner. | | `src/components/ConfirmDialog.tsx` | Modal confirmation on ``: focus starts on Cancel, Escape cancels, focus returns afterward. | | `src/routes/Community.tsx` | `/community`: public maps from `GET /api/scans/public` with their names, and loading placeholders, empty and error states. | | `src/lib/session.ts` | Stand-in signed-in account for development (`VITE_DEV_USER`, `VITE_DEV_NAME`) until real sign-in exists. | | `src/lib/preferences.tsx` | Settings kept on the device (no account needed): text size, motion, and the "Avoid stairs" default. `useTripAvoidStairs` gives each map a per-trip switch that starts from the default and doesn't change it. | | `src/routes/Settings.tsx` | `/settings`: Text size (Default, Large, Extra large), Motion (Match my device, Reduce, Allow), Avoid stairs by default. | | `src/routes/Upload.tsx` | `/maps/new` (`/upload` redirects here): an optional name (suggested from the file name), choose a PLY or GLB (checked for type, size and header before sending), pick Public, Unlisted or Private (with viewer IDs), upload with progress and cancel. | | `src/components/SharePanel.tsx` | After upload: guest link, copy, QR code, preview, and visibility changes through `PATCH /api/scans/`. Warns when the link is `localhost`, which a phone can't open. | | `src/lib/scans.ts` | Owner API client (upload, sharing) with readable messages for 400, 401, 413, 415 and network failures. | | `src/routes/GuestView.tsx` | `/s/:shareId` with loading, not-found/denied, download, parse-failure and unsupported-format (GLB) states. | ## Accessibility - **Keyboard:** "Skip to main content" is the first Tab stop in the app. On a map, Tab order is top bar, then the map, then Avoid stairs and Reset view. With the map focused, the arrow keys turn it (Shift for bigger steps), + and − zoom, and R resets. - **Focus rings** follow the surface so they stay above 3:1: forest on paper, paper on the forest menu, coral on night. Coral on paper is only 2.2:1, so it is never used for focus there. - **Text size** scales the root font (everything is in rem). At Extra large, phones show map cards one per row and the map's bottom controls wrap. - **Reduced motion** follows the device unless Settings overrides it. It turns off CSS animations and the 3D map's glide after letting go. - **Automated check:** with `pnpm dev` running, open a page and paste this in the browser console to run axe (WCAG 2.x A/AA and best practices): ```js const s = await (await fetch("/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js?raw")).text(); (0, eval)(s.replace(/^export default /, "window.__axe = ")); (0, eval)(window.__axe); (await axe.run(document)).violations ``` On 2026-11-21, `/`, `/maps`, `/community`, `/settings`, `/maps/new` (form and share panel) and `/s/` (map and not-found) returned no violations at 1280x800, and the map also at 375x812 with Extra large text. axe can't measure text over the 3D canvas, so those pairs were checked by hand: sage on night is 9.3:1 and paper on night is 14.6:1. ====== import { Link } from "react-router"; /** Placeholder until the landing page (DESIGN.md P0: landing hero) is built. */ export default function Home() { return (

Path

Scan a building, a campus or a trail, and share it as a 3D map anyone can find their way through.

Open a guest link at /s/<shareId> to view a shared scan.

Open my maps Browse community maps
); }

Coral on night is 6.7:1, which suits the route line and 3D labels. ## Type - Display: **Overpass** 800–900 (based on Highway Gothic road-sign lettering). - Body and UI: **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** (Braille Institute, designed for low-vision readers). - Data: **Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono** for coordinates, distances, share IDs. - Avoid a soft serif. Cream + coral + serif reads as a generic generated landing page. ## Motifs and motion - The landing hero is the product: the real scan assembles from scattered points, the coral route draws itself, footprints walk it to a destination pin. Use the fixture until a real scan exists. - Footprints are the landing-page motif: one SVG path in the left gutter, prints revealed with scroll (GSAP ScrollTrigger + MotionPath). Under 40% opacity. - Inside the app, routes are a coral line with flowing dashes and waypoint dots, not footprints, since some users roll rather than walk. - One orchestrated animation per landing section. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` everywhere. - Booth: a QR in the hero and Join section opens the guest link on the judge's phone. The hero replays after ~20 s idle. ## Landing page sections Hero (live scan + QR + Log in / Sign up) → The problem (sticky scroll: 2D floor plan tilts into 3D, one measured stat) → Our product (Scan · Share with Public/Unlisted/Private · Navigate with landmark cues, real screenshots) → How to use (3 steps joined by footprints) → Creators (flip cards: hover on desktop, tap on iPhone, focus on keyboard; GitHub, LinkedIn, résumé, portfolio) → Join us (trail ends at a pin by the CTA and QR). ## App screens, by priority - **P0:** guest view at `/s/:shareId` (full-bleed 3D on night, destinations in a bottom sheet, Gemini cue card with source frame and "approved by the map owner", route by Dijkstra over the manifest graph) · upload with visibility toggle, copy link and QR · Gemini cue review (accept / edit / reject) · landing hero. - **P1:** rest of the landing page · Explore (public scans + filter chips: Campus, Events, Hospitals, Trails, Step-free) · settings (step-free routing, text size, reduce motion) · one "elevator out" alert that reroutes. - **Cut or fake:** custom login screens (use the provider's hosted login), comments and feed, events calendar, live indoor positioning. ## Stack Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + React Router, built to static files. | Job | Library | | --- | --- | | 3D viewer | `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei` (PLYLoader, CameraControls, Line, Html) | | Scroll story, footprints | `gsap`, `@gsap/react` (ScrollTrigger, MotionPath, DrawSVG) | | UI motion | `motion` | | Landing smooth scroll | `lenis` (off in the app and under reduced motion) | | Components | shadcn/ui (Radix) | | Bottom sheet | `vaul` | | Toasts, QR, icons | `sonner`, `qrcode.react`, `lucide-react` | | Showpieces | Two or three restyled snippets from Magic UI, Aceternity UI or React Bits | Mobile targets: the guest link opens signed out in under 3 s on an iPhone; cap device pixel ratio at 2 and downsample large PLYs. Hosting is proposed on Vultr behind Caddy, which must serve `index.html` for `/s/` so direct links don't 404. ======== # Website Arielle owns the website: the signed-in home, upload and sharing, and the guest 3D viewer. Build the website here. Start with an upload control, the three visibility choices, a copy-link action and a guest route at `/s/`. Display upload, loading and processing failures where they occur. For the first integration, upload the sample PLY as **Unlisted**, open the returned link in a signed-out session, and use the response’s `assetPath` to load the point cloud with vertex colors. A guest should be able to orbit the scene and recognize the corridor junction. Use the actual phone export to choose camera framing, point size and mobile performance targets. The local API provides fixture bytes and exercises sharing rules. Replace its test page with the website’s guest route during integration. [Local API commands](../../services/api/README.md) · [Capture format and viewer notes](../../docs/scan-formats.md) ## Run locally Requires Node 22+ and pnpm. The dev server proxies `/api` to the scan mock on `127.0.0.1:8001`. ```sh py -3 -B tools/scan_mock.py --port 8001 # from the repo root (or: make dev-api) cd apps/web && pnpm install && pnpm dev # http://localhost:5173 ``` Open `http://localhost:5173/maps` (Your maps), then **New map** (`/maps/new`), choose `fixtures/venue/scene.ply`, pick a visibility and upload. The page shows the guest link, a copy button and a QR code, and lets you change visibility or private viewers afterwards. You can also upload with the curl command in the [API README](../../services/api/README.md). Then open `http://localhost:5173/s/`. The guest page sends no `X-Dev-User` header, so it is a signed-out guest. Owner calls (upload, sharing) send `X-Dev-User: demo-owner` in development only (override with `VITE_DEV_USER`). A production build sends none, because the hosted API reads the signed-in session. `pnpm build` type-checks and writes static files to `dist/`. `pnpm preview` serves them with the same proxy on port 4173. The host must serve `index.html` for `/s/`. | Path | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/index.css` | Color and type tokens from [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) as a Tailwind v4 `@theme`. | | `src/lib/shares.ts` | Calls `GET /api/shares/` and its asset. The API answers 404 both for unknown and for denied shares, so the guest sees one state. | | `src/lib/ply.ts` | Parses ASCII or binary PLY with `PLYLoader`, rejects empty or non-finite scans, keeps at most 600k points. | | `src/components/ScanViewer.tsx` | Colored points on `night`, DPR capped at 2, orbit (one finger turns, two fingers zoom and pan), framed from behind the entrance (+Z). Loaded lazily alongside the metadata request. | | `src/components/AppLayout.tsx` | Signed-in shell: forest sidebar (My maps, Community, New map, account) on desktop, top bar and bottom tab bar on phones. | | `src/routes/MyMaps.tsx` | `/maps`: your maps (`GET /api/scans/mine`) and maps shared with you (`GET /api/scans/shared`), with All, Public, Unlisted, Private and Shared with me filters. Each card's ⋯ menu offers Copy link, Manage map and Delete… (with a confirmation). | | `src/routes/ManageMap.tsx` | `/maps/:shareId`: rename, link and QR code, change who can open it, and delete. Only for the map's owner. | | `src/components/ConfirmDialog.tsx` | Modal confirmation on ``: focus starts on Cancel, Escape cancels, focus returns afterward. | | `src/routes/Community.tsx` | `/community`: public maps from `GET /api/scans/public` with their names, and loading placeholders, empty and error states. | | `src/lib/session.ts` | Stand-in signed-in account for development (`VITE_DEV_USER`, `VITE_DEV_NAME`) until real sign-in exists. | | `src/lib/preferences.tsx` | Settings kept on the device (no account needed): text size, motion, and the "Avoid stairs" default. `useTripAvoidStairs` gives each map a per-trip switch that starts from the default and doesn't change it. | | `src/routes/Settings.tsx` | `/settings`: Text size (Default, Large, Extra large), Motion (Match my device, Reduce, Allow), Avoid stairs by default. | | `src/routes/Upload.tsx` | `/maps/new` (`/upload` redirects here): an optional name (suggested from the file name), choose a PLY or GLB (checked for type, size and header before sending), pick Public, Unlisted or Private (with viewer IDs), upload with progress and cancel. | | `src/components/SharePanel.tsx` | After upload: guest link, copy, QR code, preview, and visibility changes through `PATCH /api/scans/`. Warns when the link is `localhost`, which a phone can't open. | | `src/lib/scans.ts` | Owner API client (upload, sharing) with readable messages for 400, 401, 413, 415 and network failures. | | `src/routes/GuestView.tsx` | `/s/:shareId` with loading, not-found/denied, download, parse-failure and unsupported-format (GLB) states. | ## Accessibility - **Keyboard:** "Skip to main content" is the first Tab stop in the app. On a map, Tab order is top bar, then the map, then Avoid stairs and Reset view. content.text:
Here's what I'd build. I've read `DESIGN.md`, the web README, the current `Home.tsx` placeholder and your playbook artifact.

## Section order

The order follows DESIGN.md. Each section gets one animation and nothing else moves in it.

1. **Top bar** (dark green band): Path logo, links that jump to each section, **Log in** (goes to `/maps`) and a coral **New map** button (goes to `/maps/new`).
2. **Hero** (dark "night" band): headline, a short sentence, buttons for Your maps, Community and New map, the live 3D scan, and a "Try it on your phone" QR code.
3. **The problem**: a flat, cluttered floor plan that tilts into the 3D scan as you scroll (a pinned "sticky" section whose tilt follows how far you've scrolled), plus one number that counts up.
4. **Our product**: three panels for Scan, Share (Public, Unlisted, Private) and Navigate (landmark cues).
5. **How to use**: three numbered steps joined by footprints.
6. **Creators**: flip cards. They flip on hover with a mouse, on tap on a phone, and on focus from the keyboard.
7. **Join us**: the footprint trail ends at a pin next to "Map your first space" and a large QR code.
8. **Footer.**

On laptops a faint footprint trail runs down the left margin (under 40% opacity) and reveals more prints as you scroll. On phones it's hidden because there's no margin for it.

## What the hero does

- The T-shaped corridor appears as scattered dots that fly together into the scan (about 2 seconds). A coral route then draws itself from the entrance to the destination, footprints walk along it, and a pin drops at the end.
- Two buttons on the scan, **Workshop room** and **Info booth**, redraw the route to that place. You can drag to turn the scan.
- After about 20 seconds with nobody touching it, it replays, so the booth laptop keeps moving between judges.
- It uses the 3D tools you already have (three.js and React Three Fiber). The 3D code loads after the text (lazy-loaded), so the headline appears right away.
- **With Reduce motion on:** the finished scene shows still, with the route and pin already drawn. There's no replay, no fly-in, no scroll tilt and no counting. The trail shows as static prints, and flip cards swap sides without turning. With Large or Extra large text, sizes grow because everything is in rem, and the hero stacks the text above the scan earlier.

## Real versus faked for the demo

| Real | Faked or placeholder |
| --- | --- |
| Every link: `/maps`, `/community`, `/maps/new` | **The hero scan.** `scene.ply` has only 93 points, too few to look like anything when they fly together. I'd generate a denser copy (a few thousand dots) from the same layout and coordinates: entrance, junction, amber workshop door, purple booth door. Swapping in the real scan later means changing one file. |
| QR code, generated live from a link you set in a config value (an environment variable, `VITE_DEMO_SHARE_URL`) | **"Log in"** goes straight to Your maps with the stand-in demo account, since real sign-in is out of scope |
| Team names and roles from the README | **The problem stat** needs a number you actually measured. Until you have one, it shows a clearly marked placeholder. |
| | **Product panels:** small live versions built from your real components (the visibility picker and a route card) instead of screenshots, which you don't have yet |
| | **Creator links and photos:** initials and placeholder links until you send real ones |

One booth gotcha: a QR code that points at `localhost` won't open on a judge's phone. It needs the hosted link or your laptop's network address.

## Libraries

**I recommend installing nothing new.** The hero reuses three.js, React Three Fiber and drei. The QR uses `qrcode.react`, which is already installed. Scroll effects use the browser's built-in way of noticing when a section is on screen (IntersectionObserver) plus a small scroll listener, and CSS transitions do the rest. That gives the fewest moving parts the night before the deadline, and the Reduce motion setting already switches off CSS motion everywhere.

DESIGN.md lists GSAP, Lenis and Motion. I'd skip Lenis entirely, because smooth scrolling that takes over the page works against your accessibility pitch. GSAP would make the footprint trail and the tilting floor plan a bit smoother. If you'd like that, I'd add only `gsap` and `@gsap/react`, picking versions older than 14 days so they pass the workspace's release-age rule.

## Two quick answers that would help (optional)

- The measured number for "The problem" (for example, how long a first-timer took to find a room), or I'll leave the marked placeholder.
- GitHub handles or links for the Creators cards. I only know yours (AryBaum).

Once you OK it, I'll branch `feature/landing-page` off `feature/manage-maps` and build it. To see it, run `pnpm dev` in `apps/web` and open `http://localhost:5173/` (or another port if 5173 is taken). I'll check it in the browser pane at laptop and phone sizes with Reduce motion on and off.

Other cool animations going around that i just dont know how or if we should incorporate are like the phone model things like where you can put your photo of the screen but like orient and animate the phone model, some have like this object that scrolls or like falls down the page as you scroll, some have like your cursor hover changes the background as you move or like leaves a trail that fades etc. Also like should it be QR codes or they make a login?

You're right about the second button. Here's the full revised plan, with your ideas folded in.

## Buttons, log in, and QR codes

You're right, two New map buttons is one too many. These are really two different people with two different needs:

- **Visitors never log in.** They scan a QR code or tap a link and the map opens straight away, with no account and no app. That's the core promise, so the hero keeps its QR code. At the booth, a judge scans it and the guest map opens on their own phone.
- **Map owners log in** to scan, label and share.

So the page gets one main action plus one browsing option:
- Top bar: **Log in** only.
- Hero: **Start mapping** (main button, goes to New map, which will ask for login once real sign-in exists) and **Explore maps** (goes to Community).

Your maps (`/maps`) is still reachable from Log in.

## The problem, told in three steps

The section walks through what people use today, why it falls short, and what Path does instead:

| What's out there | Why it isn't enough |
| --- | --- |
| Google Maps | Gets you to the building, then stops at the door. Indoor maps exist for only a few malls and airports. |
| PDF floor plans and "You are here" boards | Flat and often out of date. You can't tell a step from a ramp, and you can't carry the board with you. |
| Signs, or asking someone | Missing or inconsistent. At events, room names change every weekend. |
| "Accessible entrance available" | Doesn't say where it is or what the route looks like. |

**What Path does:** a real 3D scan you can look at before you go, routes that can avoid stairs, room labels the map owner controls, and it opens from a QR code with no account.

The animation: the flat floor plan tilts and turns into the 3D scan as you scroll. Any number on this section has to be one you actually measured; I won't make up statistics.

## New section: "Who it's for"

This goes right after the problem. I suggest four people, each shown as a simple figure in the style of a wayfinding sign (a **pictogram**, like the people on airport and road signs). That ties into the road-sign font. Hovering, tapping or tabbing to a figure makes it walk a short coral route to its destination:

1. **Students:** find your classroom or exam room on the first day. Route ends at "Room 204".
2. **People who use a wheelchair or avoid stairs:** check whether a place works for you before you leave home, and go straight to the elevator or ramp instead of searching for it. The figure is an active, forward-leaning wheelchair user who rolls the route, and the route visibly bends around a staircase. This part is real: the Avoid stairs switch already exists in the app.
3. **Event teams** like Hack Western: label rooms the way your event needs them, such as "Workshop room" or "Sponsor booth". The figure drops a label pin.
4. **Explorers:** share a trail or a campus you know. The figure walks onto a trailhead.

**One thing to check with Sam first:** you mentioned organizers labeling *an existing map* someone else made. The app doesn't do that yet (only a map's owner can edit it). If it isn't planned for the demo, I'd write "label every room on your map" so judges don't ask for something we can't show.

## Creators: a deck that splits

Yes, this works. All four cards start stacked in one pile. As you scroll in, two slide left and two slide right into an evenly spaced row, then each flips on hover, tap or keyboard focus. On phones the pile spreads into a 2x2 grid instead, because there's no room for a row. With Reduce motion on, they simply sit in their final row.

## Your other animation ideas

| Idea | My call |
| --- | --- |
| **3D phone** that turns as you scroll | **Yes, for "Our product".** A phone drawn with CSS (a **CSS 3D mockup**, so there's no licensed 3D model to worry about) tilts as you scroll through Scan, Share and Navigate, and its screen changes for each step. For Navigate, the screen shows the live scan. |
| **An object that falls down the page** | **Yes, but merged with the footprint trail.** A coral "you are here" dot travels down the trail in the margin as you scroll and lands as the destination pin at Join us. One moving thing instead of two. |
| **Cursor trail or background that follows the mouse** | **Only inside the hero:** dots in the point cloud near your cursor glow brighter. A page-wide cursor trail doesn't exist on phones, competes with the text, and bothers people sensitive to motion. That's an odd look for an accessibility product. |

All of it switches off under Reduce motion, and every hover effect also works on tap and keyboard focus.

## Revised order, and one library change

Hero → The problem → Who it's for → Our product (phone) → How to use → Creators → Join us.

With this much scroll choreography (pinning a section, tying motion to scroll position, called **scrubbing**), GSAP now earns its place. I'd add `gsap` and `@gsap/react`, picking versions older than 14 days. I'd still skip Lenis and Motion.

**Scope warning:** the deadline is tomorrow at 9 a.m., so I'd build in this order and cut from the bottom if time runs short:
1. Hero, problem, Who it's for, Join us
2. Creators deck
3. Phone
4. Cursor glow

Three things to settle before I start:
1. Is labeling someone else's map planned, or should I stick to "label your own map"?
2. Are you OK with adding GSAP?
3. Are these four people (students, wheelchair users, event teams, explorers) the right ones, or do you want others, for example hospital visitors?

content.text:
Got it. I was leaning on the README's event framing instead of the app you've actually built. Your pages already tell the right story: **Your maps** ("a building, campus or trail"), **Community** ("Public maps anyone can open, no account needed"), **New map**, **Manage map**, and the map view with **Avoid stairs**. So the landing page advertises the software itself. You log in, make your own maps or open ones the community has shared, and add waypoints. Events are just one of many uses, and that's why there are so many kinds of users.

## Revised plan

1. **Hero:** "3D maps of real places, made by the people who know them" (draft wording). The live scan assembles and a route draws itself.
   - Top bar: **Log in**.
   - Hero buttons: **Start mapping** (goes to New map, where you'll log in) and **Explore community maps** (goes to Community).
   - QR code labeled "Open a sample map on your phone". This shows the other half of the product: a shared map opens without an account.
2. **The problem:** what's out there (Google Maps stops at the door, flat floor plans, signs, vague "accessible entrance" notes), why it isn't enough, and how Path fixes it. The flat floor plan tilts into 3D as you scroll.
3. **What you can do in Path:** a tour of the real app on a phone that turns as you scroll. Each step matches a real page:
   - **Make a map:** scan a place with a LiDAR iPhone and upload it.
   - **Add waypoints and name rooms:** "Workshop room", "Sponsor booth", "Room 204", "Elevator".
   - **Share it your way:** Public (listed in Community), Unlisted (link only) or Private (people you invite), by link or QR code.
   - **Explore Community:** open maps other people have shared.
   - **Follow a route:** with Avoid stairs for that trip.
4. **Who uses it:** the same app used different ways, shown as pictogram figures that animate on hover, tap or keyboard focus. Students find classrooms and exam rooms on a community map of their campus. People who use a wheelchair or avoid stairs check a place before they go, then take the elevator or ramp route. Event teams like Hack Western map their venue and label workshop and sponsor rooms. Explorers share trails and campuses they know.
5. **How to use:** three steps joined by footprints. Log in, make or find a map, then share it or follow it.
6. **Creators:** the stacked deck that splits two left and two right, then flips.
7. **Join us:** the "you are here" dot travels down the trail and lands as a pin next to **Start mapping** and the QR code.

## Two questions

1. **Labeling someone else's map:** when an event team uses a community map they didn't scan, can they add their own room labels and waypoints, for example in their own copy? Or can only the map's owner label it? I'll word "Who uses it" to match. The waypoint and label editor isn't built yet (the roadmap has it as "connect a QR start to two destinations"), so the landing page describes it as a feature of the app without showing a real screen for it.
2. **GSAP:** the scroll effects (turning phone, splitting deck, tilting floor plan, traveling dot) need `gsap` and `@gsap/react`, using versions older than 14 days. Still no Lenis.

The search didn't turn up a Codrops tutorial specifically on stacked cards that spread on scroll. The closest Codrops hit is a breakdown of a portfolio site's card animations that uses Locomotive Scroll rather than ScrollTrigger, so it's less relevant. The GSAP-based examples are more useful.

- **CodePen stacking demo:** One example pins a `.stack` container and scales each card down by index, using a negative `marginBottom` so the cards overlap. Each card's scroll range is set with `start` and `end` values, and the pinned cards use `pinSpacing: false`. (codepen.io/v-dj/pen/xxPvdzK)

- **Spread/unstack example:** A GSAP forum thread asks about mimicking an effect where cards unstack on scroll, and a RoshitShrestha CodePen uses a timeline that toggles a stacked class and uses Flip on scroll to spread the cards into a grid. (codepen.io/RoshitShrestha/pen/pvbNRQd)

Your usage limit was reached, so I stopped partway. Every landing page section is written and saved as a WIP commit, `067d1bb` on `feature/landing-page`. The type check passes, but I've only seen the hero in the browser. I haven't run axe or `pnpm build`, and nothing is pushed.

**What's built** (in `apps/web/src/landing/`):
- **Hero:** I checked this one at 1280x800. The scan flies together from scattered dots, then a coral route draws itself with footprints, and a pin drops at the door.
  - The **Workshop room** and **Info booth** buttons redraw the route.
  - Dots near your mouse glow.
  - It replays after 20 seconds idle, which you can also trigger with **Replay**.
  - The QR code opens a sample map. It points at Community until you set `VITE_DEMO_SHARE_URL` to a hosted guest link, because a phone can't open `localhost`.
- **The problem:** four road-sign panels. As you scroll, the floor plan stays on screen (pinned), tilts, and its walls rise into 3D before a route draws across it.
- **What you can do in Path:** a phone drawn in CSS that turns as you scroll. Its screen steps through Scan, Waypoints, Share, Community and Route, beside a transit-line stepper.
- **Who it's for:** one big green wayfinding sign. Pictogram figures walk or roll to Room 204, the elevator (skipping the stairs), a sponsor booth and a trailhead.
- **How to use:** three numbered highway-style shields joined by footprints that appear as you scroll.
- **Creators:** the four cards start in one pile and spread out two left and two right as you scroll. Each card flips on hover, with a Flip button on phones, or when its links get keyboard focus.
- **Join us** and a footer.
- I added `gsap` and `@gsap/react` for the scroll effects, both versions older than 14 days.

**What's left:**
- Check every section below the hero in the browser at 1280x800 and 375x812, with Reduce motion on and off and with Extra large text. Then fix what turns up and run axe on `/` and `pnpm build`.
- Build the footprint trail in the left margin, with the "you are here" dot travelling down the page.
- Replace the WIP commit with a proper one, then ask you before creating the issue, pushing, or opening the PR stacked on `feature/manage-maps`.

**Decision for you:** the event teams row says they can "start from a map someone already shared". The app can't do that yet, so keep the line only if it's planned.

**To see it:** I can't start the server for you. It runs in Claude's browser pane on port 5174, using a local config file (`.claude/launch.json`) that isn't committed. Use 5174 because another dev server is already on 5173. In `apps/web`, run:
```powershell
pnpm exec vite --port 5174
```
Then open `http://localhost:5174/`.

The handoff note with all of this is in the shared notes folder as `landing-page-handoff.md`.

Ideas I drew on:
- [Maxime Heckel on R3F particles](https://blog.maximeheckel.com/posts/the-magical-world-of-particles-with-react-three-fiber-and-shaders/) for the flying dots.
- [Codrops on stacked CSS layers](https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/03/03/css-meets-voxel-art-building-a-rendering-engine-with-stacked-grids/) for the rising walls.
- [GSAP's stacking-cards thread](https://gsap.com/community/forums/topic/39367-scrolltrigger-stacking-cards-animation-logic-to-create-any-effect-yes-even-yours/) and a [card spread CodePen](https://codepen.io/RoshitShrestha/pen/pvbNRQd) for the Creators pile.

content.text:
I rebuilt the hero to follow your reference layout and committed it as `c799ef0` on `feature/landing-page`.

**What changed:**
- **One open night sky.** The top bar is see-through over the hero and only turns frosted once you scroll. A soft green glow comes from the top corners, with a faint coral warmth under the route and a few twinkling stars.
- **Centered headline, less clutter.** "See the turn before you reach it." with one short line under it, a single cream **Start mapping** button, and a quiet **Explore community maps →** link beside it. The small label above the heading (the eyebrow) is gone. The top bar has just Path, the section links and **Log in**, so there's no second New map button.
- **The scan is the big object.** It now spans the full width and rises from the bottom edge, fading into the sky at the top like the shape in your reference. Everything you had still works: the dots fly together, the route draws with footprints, dots glow under your mouse, it turns when you drag with a mouse, and it replays after 20 seconds idle.
- **Floating frosted panels instead of cards.** On the left, **Route to** holds Workshop room or Info booth, a replay button, and the live distance. On the right, **Try it on your phone** holds the QR code. Both drift slowly up and down. On phones the QR panel is hidden, since you're already on a phone, and the route panel sits under the scan.

**What I checked:**
- In the browser pane at 1280x800 and 375x812, the text stays clear of the scan.
- With Reduce motion on, the finished scene appears straight away and nothing floats or twinkles.
- axe found 0 violations on `/`.
- I haven't re-run `pnpm build`.

**Not changed yet:** the sections below the hero are still the earlier boxy version. Your notes about eyebrows and the page feeling too divided into blocks apply there next.

To see it, refresh `http://localhost:5174/` in the browser pane.

content.text:
I fixed all four things and committed them as `0fc7a84`. Refresh `http://localhost:5174/` to see them.

- **Smaller headline, nothing on top of the scan:** the headline is about a fifth smaller. The scan now sits in its own space below the text instead of behind it, so the buttons and the sentence under the headline stay readable.
- **Start mapping is coral** with dark text and a soft coral glow. White text on coral would fail contrast, so the text is dark.
- **No abrupt ending:** the scan fades out at the bottom as well as the top, and the hero now ends in a big rounded edge before the next section instead of a hard cut. I also moved the two floating panels further out so they don't cover the scan.
- **Phone:** the Route to panel now has space below it before the rounded edge.

I checked it at 1900x1000 (close to your screenshot), 1280x800 and 375x812. The horizontal scrollbar in your screenshot belongs to the browser pane's size setting, not the page; the page itself is no wider than the window. `pnpm build` passes.

axe found no problems in the hero. It did flag faint text in the old "Problem" section below: those signs are dimmed while they wait their turn in the scroll animation. That section is next on the list anyway, along with removing the eyebrow labels and making the page flow instead of feeling like separate blocks.

The hero now fits on one screen with nothing cut off, and the scan is big again. It's committed as `18d00ac`; refresh `http://localhost:5174/` to see it.

- **Smaller text block:** the headline is one line on a laptop ("See the turn before you reach it."), the sentence under it is a size smaller, and the Start mapping button is a bit more compact.

content.text:
Starting the server from VS Code won't fix this on its own. The problem is almost certainly the network, not the server.

**What I found:**
- Your laptop is on the **uwo.ca** campus Wi-Fi.
- Windows Firewall already allows Node on that type of network, so the firewall isn't what's blocking your phone.
- Campus networks like this usually stop devices from talking to each other (called **client isolation**), so your phone can't reach your laptop even on the same Wi-Fi.

Two ways around it:

**1. Phone hotspot (quickest, nothing to install)**
1. On your iPhone, turn on **Settings → Personal Hotspot**.
2. Connect the laptop to the iPhone's hotspot.
3. Tell me once it's connected. The laptop will get a new address (usually `172.20.10.something`), and I'll give you the exact link to open in Safari.

**2. VS Code port forwarding (works on any network)**
This is where VS Code does help: it can make a temporary public web address that leads to the server on your laptop.
1. Open the **Ports** panel (next to Terminal).
2. Click **Forward a Port**, type `5175`, and sign in with GitHub when asked.
3. Right-click the port, choose **Port Visibility → Public**, and open the forwarded address in Safari.

Vite blocks unfamiliar web addresses by default, so I'd need to add a one-line setting to `vite.config.ts` that allows VS Code's forwarded addresses (`.devtunnels.ms`). Anyone with that link could open your dev site while forwarding is on, so turn it off when you're done.

customTitle: Plan and build the Path landing page

content.text:
Agreed. The scroll-locked version was the wrong call, especially on phones. Here's how I'd rebuild it.

## Why the other options fall short

The section should answer one question: **"Google Maps exists, so why Path?"** The honest answer has six parts:

| What people use | Where it stops |
| --- | --- |
| **Google or Apple Maps** | Gets you to the building, then stops. Indoors, GPS drifts and the building is usually a grey box. |
| **Their indoor maps** | Exist mostly for big airports and malls, and only the venue owner can add one. Your lecture building, a hospital wing or this weekend's venue usually has none. |
| **PDF floor plans and wall boards** | Flat, often years out of date, and they don't show what the turn actually looks like. |
| **"Accessible entrance ✓"** | A yes or no tag on a listing, not a route. You find the stairs when you reach them. |
| **Events** | Rooms get new names every weekend, and nobody can relabel someone else's map. |
| **Path** | Anyone can scan a place with a phone. You see the real place in 3D, follow a step-free route, and it opens from a link or QR code, with no GPS needed. |

The key point for judges: Google has the features, but only for places that partner with it. **Path lets the people who know a place map it themselves.**

## The design: a short loop that plays itself

No pinned scrolling. The page scrolls normally, and the section is one dark rounded "screen" in the hero's style (night background, frosted panels, coral route). It plays one story on a loop: **"Getting to Room 204."** Each scene shows a tool failing at a specific moment, then Path solves it:

1. **Map app:** the blue dot arrives at the building, then wobbles inside a grey box. Caption: *"GPS gets you to the door. Inside, it drifts."*
2. **Indoor maps:** a short list where the airport and the mall light up, but "Science building" is greyed out: *"No indoor map."*
3. **Floor plan:** a flat, cluttered PDF with "REV. 2014" and a renamed room: *"Room 1.12? It's 1.04 now."*
4. **"Accessible entrance ✓":** a route draws straight into a staircase, which flashes: *"A checkmark, not a route."*
5. **Path:** the same building as a 3D scan (the hero's dots, drawn simply). The coral route goes around the stairs to the elevator and Room 204, with a cue card: *"Take the elevator, then left at the amber door."*

**How it behaves:**
- A row of **tabs** under the screen (Map app · Indoor maps · Floor plan · Accessibility tag · Path) shows which scene is playing and fills like a progress bar. Click any tab to jump to it.
- It plays only while it's on screen. It pauses on hover or keyboard focus, and has a **Pause** button. Accessibility rules require a way to stop content that moves on its own for more than 5 seconds.
- **With Reduce motion on:** no autoplay. Each tab shows its finished scene as a still.
- **Phones:** same screen at full width, tabs scroll sideways, and the caption sits under the screen so nothing is ever cut off.
- It's built with plain SVG and CSS, with no 3D engine and no scroll tracking, so it stays light on phones.

## The summary under the loop

One clean comparison strip, so a judge can read the whole argument in five seconds:
- Six needs as rows: *works inside any building, anyone can map it, shows what it looks like, step-free route inside, labels you can change, opens from a link*.
- Columns for **Map apps · Floor plans · Path**.
- Simple filled and empty dots, with only the Path column in coral.

It's text, so screen readers and axe can read it, unlike the old faded signs.

The headline is centered like the hero, with no eyebrow label: **"Maps stop at the front door."** A one-line subtitle goes under it.

Two things I'd like your call on:
1. **Naming Google:** the captions say "map apps" and only mention Google and Apple by name in the indoor-maps scene, which is accurate and less confrontational. Or do you want Google named throughout?
2. **The comparison strip:** keep it under the loop, or let the loop carry the message alone and keep the page less busy?

If this direction works, I'll build it in place of the current Problem section.
